newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Bosnia bids U.N. delay lifting Yugoslav sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia bids U.N. delay lifting Yugoslav sanctions.

text.p: Bosnia's government urged the U.N. Security Council on Wednesday to delay lifting sanctions imposed on the rump Yugoslav state, saying it had not yet complied with provisions of the Dayton peace deal.
Bosnia's U.N. representative, Mohamed Sacirbey, made the appeal in a letter to the Security Council.
Russia had wanted the sanctions against Serbia and Montenegro -- suspended following the Dayton peace agreement, which ended the Bosnian war last year -- lifted on Tuesday.
But the Security Council took no action, chiefly because the United States said it wanted the Sept. 14 elections in Bosnia to be formally certified first.
Sacirbey wrote that rump Yugoslavia had refused to establish normal diplomatic relations with Bosnia and had not cooperated fully with the war crimes tribunal in The Hague.
There had also been voter manipulation, so the elections could not be considered free and fair, he wrote.
"The Security Council should extract the necessary compliance ... before granting further concessions," he wrote.

Sanctions against the Yugoslav state of Serbia and Montegro were suspended by the council last November as a followup to the U.S.-initiated Balkan peace accords signed in Dayton, Ohio. The council's resolution stipulated that the sanctions would be lifted entirely 10 days after the Bosnian elections, which to Moscow meant Sept. 24.

But the United States has interpreted the resolution as saying the 10-day countdown should begin after the the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) had certified the elections in writing.
Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic, who will chair his country's new three-member presidency, was due to address the U.N. General Assembly in New York later on Wednesday.
